title: LLM Inference Acceleration Architecture Intern - Moe & Attention-FFN Disaggregation
description: Please Note: To provide the best candidate experience amidst our high application volumes, each candidate is limited to 10 applications across all open jobs within a 6-month period. Advancing the World’s Technology Together Our technology solutions power the tools you use every day--including smartphones, electric vehicles, hyperscale data centers, IoT devices, and so much more. Here, you’ll have an opportunity to be part of a global leader whose innovative designs are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and powering the future. We believe innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We’re dedicated to empowering people to be their true selves. Together, we’re building a better tomorrow for our employees, customers, partners, and communities. What You’ll Learn Project Overview: Modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs spend most of their serving cost in the decode phase, where attention is bound by KV-cache memory bandwidth while expert FFNs need dense compute. You will investigate Attention–FFN Disaggregation (AFD) — running attention and MoE experts on separately scaled resources and pipelining micro-batches between them — on NUMA systems, where memory locality and interconnect topology decide whether disaggregation pays off. You will characterize real workloads, build a performance model, prototype NUMA-aware placement and scheduling in an open-source serving framework, and turn the results into hardware–software co-design recommendations for memory and interconnect. Skills You’ll Learn: Performance characterization and modeling of LLM inference (roofline, trace-driven simulation) on multi-socket / multi-GPU NUMA systems Disaggregated serving system design: prefill–decode and attention–FFN disaggregation, MoE expert parallelism, and communication–computation overlap Hardware–software co-design: translating workload behavior into memory-hierarchy (HBM, CXL) and interconnect architecture requirements What You’ll Do The AGI team at Samsung Semiconductor explores system architectures for next-generation AI infrastructure. We co-design memory, interconnect, and software to make large-scale LLM inference faster and more cost-efficient, and our work informs Samsung’s future memory and system products. As an intern, you will own a research-driven project end to end — from profiling and modeling to prototyping — working closely with architects and systems engineers, and you will present your findings to the broader organization at the end of the summer. Location: Daily onsite presence at our San Jose headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work policy Reports to: Director Characterize decode-phase behavior of state-of-the-art MoE LLMs (e.g., DeepSeek-V3/R1, Qwen3-MoE class models) on the team’s NUMA testbed, using profilers such as Nsight Systems, PyTorch Profiler, and Linux perf. Build and validate an analytical or trace-driven performance model of Attention–FFN Disaggregation, capturing attention:expert ratios, micro-batch pipelining, all-to-all communication, and memory placement. Design and prototype NUMA-aware placement and scheduling of attention (KV-cache) and expert workers in an open-source serving framework such as vLLM or SGLang. Implement and evaluate communication–computation overlap techniques (e.g., ping-pong micro-batching, expert-parallel dispatch/combine) and measure their impact on throughput and latency SLOs. Explore the hardware design space — memory bandwidth and capacity, HBM vs. CXL-attached memory tiers, and interconnect bandwidth/latency — and quantify which knobs matter most for disaggregated MoE inference. Collaborate weekly with your mentor and with architecture and systems engineers, sharing results in team meetings and incorporating feedback into the next iteration. Communicate your findings through a final presentation and technical report, contributing to Samsung’s AI system architecture roadmap and potential publications or patents. Complete other responsibilities as assigned. What You Bring Pursuing a Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a related field preferred. Must have at least 1 academic quarter/semester remaining Solid understanding of Transformer/LLM inference, including attention and KV cache, Mixture-of-Experts, and the prefill vs. decode phases. Preferred: background in computer architecture or systems (memory hierarchy, NUMA, interconnects, performance analysis), with strong programming skills in Python and C++ and experience with PyTorch. Preferred: hands-on experience with LLM serving frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM), GPU kernel development (CUDA/Triton), or distributed communication libraries (NCCL, NVSHMEM, DeepEP). Preferred: experience with performance modeling or architecture simulation, and/or publications in venues such as ISCA, MICRO, HPCA, ASPLOS, OSDI, or MLSys. You’re inclusive, adapting your style to the situation and diverse global norms of our people. An avid learner, you approach challenges with curiosity and resilience, seeking data to help build understanding. You’re collaborative, building relationships, humbly offering support and openly welcoming approaches. Innovative and creative, you proactively explore new ideas and adapt quickly to change. #LI-AD1 What We Offer The pay range below is for all roles at this level across all US locations and functions. Pay within this range varies by work location and may also depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This is in addition to our diverse package of benefits centered around the wellbeing of our employees and their loved ones. In addition to the usual Medical/Dental/Vision, our inclusive rewards plan empowers our people to care for their whole selves. An investment in your future is an investment in ours. Relocation Support Live 50+ miles away from your new office? No worries! We'll provide a stipend to help support your move. Housing Stipend Signing a lease on a new place for your summer internship? We'll help you pay your way with a monthly stipend. Give Back With a charitable giving match and frequent opportunities to get involved, we take an active role in supporting the community. Prioritize Emotional Wellness With on-demand apps and paid therapy sessions, you’ll have support no matter where you are. Stay Fit Eating well and being active are important parts of a healthy life. Our onsite Café and gym, plus virtual classes, make it easier. Embrace Flexibility Benefits are best when you have the space to use them. That’s why we facilitate a flexible environment so you can find the right balance for you. title: Research Intern - CXL Memory
description: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. You'll join the Compute System Architecture (CSA) team in the System Planning and Architecture (SPARC) organization, part of Azure Hardware Systems & Infrastructure (AHSI). CSA evaluates new server technologies for Azure across compute, memory, storage and interconnect. We're looking for a Research Intern to study memory pooling and sharing with Compute Express Link (CXL). Pooling memory across servers can improve memory use and let applications on different servers share data. You'll run workloads on CXL memory pools in our lab and measure how operating systems, file systems and applications perform. You'll then document the tradeoffs to help shape future Azure platforms. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Additional Responsibilities Set up and characterize CXL memory pools: latency, bandwidth, and behavior when multiple hosts compete for the pool. Run and profile memory-intensive workloads, such as in-memory databases and analytics, on pooled and shared memory. Compare their performance and cost with local DRAM. Evaluate how operating-system, file-system and application choices affect performance, keeping shared data consistent across hosts, and reliability. Examples include memory tiering, data placement, and memory-mapped and shared-memory interfaces. Prototype software and configuration optimizations and recommend joint hardware/software design changes. Work with workload owners across Microsoft and with industry partners. Document and present your findings, with opportunities to publish. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, STEM, or a relevant field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. Preferred Qualifications Research experience in computer architecture, memory systems, operating systems or databases; publications at top venues are a plus. Hands-on experience with CXL, tiered or disaggregated memory, or NUMA performance tuning. Proficient in C/C++ and Python; experience with Linux memory management or kernel work. Experience with performance tools such as perf, VTune or Intel Memory Latency Checker, and with workload benchmarking. Clear communication, curiosity and a bias for hands-on experimentation. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. title: Research Intern - AI Systems Architecture and Efficient LLM Inference
description: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The AI Systems Architecture group at Microsoft is seeking Research Interns with skills in machine learning and computer architecture, with experience in efficient Large Language Model (LLM) inference (e.g., speculative decoding, sparse attention, KV-cache optimization), GPU architecture and kernel development, hardware performance analysis or large-scale LLM serving. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Preferred Qualifications Experience building and evaluating research prototypes or production systems for LLM inference. Proficient programming skills in Python and C++/CUDA, with hands-on experience in systems software such as inference engines, GPU kernels or runtime schedulers. Experience in at least one of the following areas: Speculative decoding: draft-model, self-speculative or multi-token-prediction (MTP) methods. Sparse or efficient attention: KV-cache selection, long-context attention, and KV-cache compression. GPU kernels and performance: CUDA or Triton kernel development, FlashAttention-style kernels, memory hierarchy and bandwidth analysis, CUDA graphs. LLM serving systems: vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or similar; batching, scheduling, paged KV-cache management and memory budgeting. Large-scale inference: tensor, expert or pipeline parallelism, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference, and multi-GPU communication. Experience with rigorous experimental methodology: designing controlled benchmarks (e.g., batch-size and context-length sweeps), profiling with tools such as Nsight Systems or Nsight Compute, and explaining performance through analysis of hardware-software interactions. Familiarity with state-of-the-art research on speculative decoding, sparse attention and efficient LLM inference, shown through research projects, publications, open-source contributions or industry experience. title: Masters AI Rack/Cluster Design Engineering Co-op
description: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology can change lives for the better. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don t shy away from humanity s challenges but are determined to help solve them. AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger technology that moves the world forward. As an AMD co-op, you ll be placed at the epicenter of the AI ecosystem, working alongside experts and industry pioneers. You ll do important work, learn new skills, expand your network, and gain real-world experience on projects that impact millions of end-users worldwide. Whether you re an undergrad or a PhD student, your contributions matter and your experience here will be a launchpad for what comes next JOB DETAILS: Location: Austin, TX, USA Onsite/Hybrid: Onsite. This is an onsite position, and the co-op is required to relocate if necessary and work full-time, 40 hours per week, from the Austin office. Duration: January 25, 2027 to August 13, 2027 WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING: We are seeking a Graduate Engineering Intern to support the design and evaluation of next-generation AI and High-Performance Computing infrastructure. In this role, you will work alongside experienced system architects and cluster engineers to analyze compute, networking, storage, power, and rack-level technologies that enable large-scale AI deployments. We will involve you in evaluating AI and HPC cluster architectures, including compute, storage, networking, and infrastructure components. You will assist with performance modeling, benchmarking, and analysis of cluster configurations, including CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, memory systems, and interconnect technologies. We will train you to study AI cluster networking technologies and analyze how bandwidth, latency, and scalability impact AI and HPC workloads. Your responsibilities will include evaluating distributed storage technologies, such as Lustre, Ceph, parallel file systems, and object storage solutions. You will support rack-level infrastructure studies involving power delivery, cabling, serviceability, scalability, and data center rack integration concepts. You will analyze benchmark, simulation, and test data to create visualizations, reports, and recommendations that support proof-of-concept validation activities. You will collaborate with hardware, networking, firmware, software, thermal, mechanical, and data center teams while contributing to technical reviews, presentations, and engineering documentation. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR: You are currently pursuing a Master s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Your expected graduation date is within 12 to 24 months of the internship start date. You have a strong academic background in one or more of the following areas: computer architecture, networking, operating systems, distributed systems, or high-performance computing. You have experience with programming or scripting languages such as Python, C/C++, Bash, or similar languages. You have familiarity with Linux environments, command-line tools, performance analysis, benchmarking, or engineering research. You have interest or exposure in AI infrastructure, HPC, cluster computing, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, or modern CPU and GPU architectures. You have an understanding of networking fundamentals, including Ethernet, TCP/IP, RDMA concepts, or InfiniBand concepts. Course projects, research, internships, open-source contributions, or engineering competitions involving AI/ML systems, distributed computing, data center infrastructure, computer architecture, PCIe, UALink, Ethernet, InfiniBand, or GPU computing are a plus. title: Design Verification, Intern Summer 2027
description: Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads. Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter! If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders. Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light! About this job Are you ready to do meaningful internship work on technology that is changing how AI systems are built? We are hiring an intern for our Design Verification team at Lightmatter! Our optical interconnect architectures leverage the unique properties of light to enable fast and efficient inference and training engines. You’ll learn how to use UVM to co-verify complex digital, analog, and photonic systems while working with a talented and passionate team of engineers across the company. Responsibilities: Collaborate closely with digital, photonics, and analog designers to gain a thorough understanding of their designs and formulate comprehensive test plans for verifying their work. Create UVM test benches for subsystem-level verification and provide support for full-chip verification. Debug test benches, identify and address issues, achieve high coverage, and ultimately sign off on Design Verification (DV). Develop Real Number Models (RNM) for photonics and analog Intellectual Properties (IPs) and conduct AMS verification to ensure accurate model representation. Integrate the RNM models seamlessly into the UVM test bench. Requirements: Currently enrolled in a Graduate Engineering program such as Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or ECE degree Proficiency in Hardware Description Languages (HDL) such as SystemVerilog Knowledge of verification methodologies such as UVM Proficiency in using simulation tools like Xcelium, ModelSim, Questa, or VCS Experience with a general purpose programming language: C/C++, Python, etc. Strong problem-solving skills to identify and resolve issues in the design Fluency in English, both written and verbal Ability to work with diverse teams of engineers and scientists Willingness and curiosity to learn from an exciting team! Preferred Qualifications: Exposure to AMS verification Exposure to formal verification Experience using Ai tools for technical use Basic Git experience and familiarity Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay determined based on the position and your location, year in school, degree, and experience. Hourly Rate in USD $53 $57 USD Benefits Comprehensive Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental Vision) Retirement Savings Matching Program Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary AD D) Generous Time Off (Vacation, Sick Public Holidays) Paid Family Leave Short Term Long Term Disability Training Development Commuter Benefits Flexible, hybrid workplace model Equity grants (applicable to full-time employees) Benefits eligibility may vary depending on your employment status and location. Lightmatter recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law. Export Control Candidates should have capacity to comply with the federally mandated requirements of U.S. export control laws.

title: Spring/Summer 2027 Masters AI Rack/Cluster Design Engineering Co-Op
description: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology can change lives for the better. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we’re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don’t shy away from humanity’s challenges but are determined to help solve them. AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. As an AMD co-op, you’ll be placed at the epicenter of the AI ecosystem, working alongside experts and industry pioneers. You’ll do important work, learn new skills, expand your network, and gain real-world experience on projects that impact millions of end-users worldwide. Whether you’re an undergrad or a PhD student, your contributions matter—and your experience here will be a launchpad for what comes next JOB DETAILS: Location: Austin, TX, USA Onsite/Hybrid: Onsite. This is an onsite position, and the co-op is required to relocate if necessary and work full-time, 40 hours per week, from the Austin office. Duration: January 25, 2027 to August 13, 2027 WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING: We are seeking a Graduate Engineering Intern to support the design and evaluation of next-generation AI and High-Performance Computing infrastructure. In this role, you will work alongside experienced system architects and cluster engineers to analyze compute, networking, storage, power, and rack-level technologies that enable large-scale AI deployments. We will involve you in evaluating AI and HPC cluster architectures, including compute, storage, networking, and infrastructure components. You will assist with performance modeling, benchmarking, and analysis of cluster configurations, including CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, memory systems, and interconnect technologies. We will train you to study AI cluster networking technologies and analyze how bandwidth, latency, and scalability impact AI and HPC workloads. Your responsibilities will include evaluating distributed storage technologies, such as Lustre, Ceph, parallel file systems, and object storage solutions. You will support rack-level infrastructure studies involving power delivery, cabling, serviceability, scalability, and data center rack integration concepts. You will analyze benchmark, simulation, and test data to create visualizations, reports, and recommendations that support proof-of-concept validation activities. You will collaborate with hardware, networking, firmware, software, thermal, mechanical, and data center teams while contributing to technical reviews, presentations, and engineering documentation. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR: You are currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Your expected graduation date is within 12 to 24 months of the internship start date. You have a strong academic background in one or more of the following areas: computer architecture, networking, operating systems, distributed systems, or high-performance computing. You have experience with programming or scripting languages such as Python, C/C++, Bash, or similar languages. You have familiarity with Linux environments, command-line tools, performance analysis, benchmarking, or engineering research. You have interest or exposure in AI infrastructure, HPC, cluster computing, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, or modern CPU and GPU architectures. You have an understanding of networking fundamentals, including Ethernet, TCP/IP, RDMA concepts, or InfiniBand concepts. Course projects, research, internships, open-source contributions, or engineering competitions involving AI/ML systems, distributed computing, data center infrastructure, computer architecture, PCIe, UALink, Ethernet, InfiniBand, or GPU computing are a plus. title: Runtime Engineer Intern
location: Austin, Texas, United States; San Jose, California, United States
description: SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value. About the SambaNova Summer 2027 Internship Program At SambaNova, our internship program is designed to give you hands-on experience tackling meaningful engineering challenges with real product impact. Because we are continuously evolving our program to provide the best possible experience, specific details and programming may vary by team and location, though you can generally expect the following: Program Structure Duration: Our summer internships are structured as a 12-week experience, kicking off with onboarding and orientation, followed by mid-program check-ins, and wrapping up with final project presentations to your team and key stakeholders. Dedicated Mentorship: To support your growth, interns are typically paired with both a manager and a peer host/mentor who provide structured mentorship, technical guidance, and project alignment throughout the summer. Locations Onsite Experience: Roles are based onsite at one of our global hubs— including San Jose (HQ), Austin, Bangalore, or Stockholm—to foster direct collaboration, community, and hands-on exposure to our teams and technology. (Note: Specific location availability varies by role.) Community Engagement: Depending on your location and cohort schedule, programming may include leadership fireside chats, workshops, hackathons, lab tours, and social outings to help you connect with fellow interns and leaders across the company. Feedback Future Opportunities: Throughout the program, you will receive structured feedback on your technical depth, ownership, collaboration, and project impact. High-performing interns may be considered for returning internships or full time opportunities upon graduation, subject to business needs and performance. About the Team The Runtime team owns the lowest level of the SambaNova software stack, the layer that talks directly to the hardware. We build the user libraries, drivers, networking, and system tools that run ML training and inference across SambaStack and SambaCloud. About the Role As a Runtime Engineer Intern, you'll write code in C/C++/Rust and Python on a scoped project across drivers, user space libraries, networking, or system tools. You'll get exposure to driver bring-up on next generation silicon, help test runtime features on large multi-node systems, and learn how to track down performance bottlenecks alongside the hardware and compiler teams. A dedicated mentor will guide you throughout the internship. Responsibilities Contribute to kernel drivers for next generation SambaNova silicon Help build user space libraries that make efficient use of hardware resources Investigate networking bottlenecks within and across nodes Build or extend tools for profiling, debugging, and job and hardware management Help test runtime features on large multi-node systems Work with the hardware and compiler teams to diagnose performance issues Present your project results to the team at the end of your internship Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field Solid programming skills in C/C++/Rust and Python Coursework or project experience with high speed networking such as RDMA, RoCE, or InfiniBand Familiarity with distributed communication libraries such as MPI, NCCL, or UCX Exposure to writing Linux kernel drivers or other system level software Experience with Linux anddebugging tools such as GDB Preferred Qualifications Pursuing an M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field Familiarity with PCIe Experience with profiling or performance analysis tools Prior internship or research experience in systems software, networking, or performance engineering Open source project ownership or contributions Submission Guidelines Please note that in order to be considered an applicant for any position at SambaNova Systems, you must submit an application form for each position for which you believe you are qualified. EEO Policy SambaNova Systems is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard basis of age (40 and over), color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, national origin/ancestry, race, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding), sexual orientation, and any other applicable status protected by federal, state, or local laws. Benefits Summary for US-Based, Full-Time Employment Positions SambaNova offers a competitive total rewards package, including the base salary, plus equity and benefits. We cover 95% premium coverage for employee medical insurance, and 77% premium coverage for dependents and offer a Health Savings Account (HSA) with employer contribution. We also offer Dental, Vision, Short/Long term Disability, Basic Life, Voluntary Life, and AD D insurance plans in addition to Flexible Spending Account (FSA) options like Health Care, Limited Purpose, and Dependent Care. Our library of well-being benefits available to you and your dependents includes a full subscription to Headspace, Gympass+ membership with access to physical gyms, One Medical membership, counseling services with an Employee Assistance Program, and much more.

title: Associate Project Manager Apprentice
description: At IBM Infrastructure & Technology, we design and operate the systems that keep the world running. title: Battery Engineer Intern - Battery Systems Engineering
description: At Meta Reality Labs, our goal is to explore, innovate and design the hardware for the next generation of AI glasses, wearables, and virtual, augmented, and mixed reality experiences. The mission of the battery team is to develop power sources for the devices that enable these experiences. We are looking for a motivated Battery Systems Engineering Intern to join our team. In this role, you will work with our battery systems engineers on the electronics, firmware configuration, and validation that turn lithium-ion cells into safe, accurate, and reliable batteries. Projects can span battery management unit (BMU) circuit design, fuel gauge configuration, evaluation of new fuel gauge and protection ICs, performance benchmarking and debug of BMUs and battery packs in both module and system level testing scenarios. This internship combines hands-on lab work, AI-driven test automation and data analysis, and collaboration across battery and hardware engineering teams. Our internships is twelve (12) weeks long and we have various start dates.

We're creating a culture where people can thrive, bold ideas can grow, and together we can shape what's next. Support the delivery of robust crack growth prediction capabilities for structural analysis. Strong background in computational mechanics. Strong technical knowledge and practical experience in numerical analysis. In-depth understanding of finite element formulations or other numerical simulation methods. Ability to overcome technical obstacles and drive assigned projects through completion. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to work collaboratively across teams and geographies. title: Mechatronic Apprentice I
description: Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey! About the Role: As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement. You will be paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. You will be expected to complete work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out your work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations. You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. You must have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate your activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role. Key job responsibilities Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to: • You will perform preventative/predictive maintenance of conveyance equipment using the appropriate job plans, procedures, and manuals. • You will conduct maintenance and basic troubleshooting of robotics and robotic work cells. • You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all material handling equipment components. • You will maintain and troubleshoot motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc. • You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head Program Requirements: • Flexible to relocate after completion of the program • Able to enroll in and attend a 9-week training at one of four designated training providers (Location to be determined post-interview) • Meet the minimum qualifying score on a Mechanical Aptitude Test Please note that while we strive to accommodate employees' preferences for shift assignments, due to operational requirements and scheduling constraints, we cannot guarantee a specific shift assignment. - Technical college or trade qualification or equivalent, or 1+ years of Amazon RME (Reliability Maintenance Engineering) experience, or 2+ years of military service (E-2+) experience - training course or certification approved by Amazon (including Career Choice and RME programs) Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.
